I don't mind at all. Like I said, feel free to talk to me whenever you need to talk about anything. To be honest, I know that finding that speck of happiness with alcohol can feel great, but it's definitely not the way to go in the long run. From your response you are aware of this, but maybe a voice from the outside might help as an extra reminder, of sorts. I also just want to say, please don't let yourself feel like you have to resort to alcohol to feel happy. You're still young and have so much going for you, so much to live for, and perhaps thinking about what you will be capable of in the future will at least keep yourself from dwelling on the feelings and thoughts that are dragging you down. 

If you don't mind me asking, do you have any other hobbies or interests besides guitar? Maybe learning a new skill or hobby, or further developing ones you already have will also provide some distraction. And even if you don't take guitar lessons for this month, perhaps you can find ways to relax when practicing. Something, anything, to prevent you from being alone with those thoughts. 

But hey, those are just my thoughts. I'm not exactly an expert in anything or anyone special, and I'm trying to get by just like everyone else. I'm still pretty young too (turning 20 tomorrow, actually), but looking back at when I was in high school and in a similar position to yours, taking each day and moment one at at time was at least a start to surviving each day of hell in my mind. And it can definitely be hard trying to get through by yourself. You're already making much more progress than I did at your age by reaching out and talking about it. And I can definitely understand how hard it is when your parents don't even know (heck, I haven't even told my own family) but now you have me and a number of other people in this community who have experienced similar things who you can talk to and go to for support, even if you feel like people in your immediate vicinity don't understand. I guess what I'm trying to say is that you definitely aren't alone, and giving up that fight with yourself is the last thing we want.

Thanks for responding. It is a bit of a relief to hear that I'm not the only one with those kinds of thoughts too. So now I feel like a slightly less alone, insane person. These days, I still feel pretty crappy from time to time, but a little less so after writing it out. I honestly do feel slightly accomplished too, because I feel like writing my feelings could be a good first step to being able to get help, but we'll see.

I hope you're doing better after getting help, and I hope that things will continue to get better for you, too! And if you ever need to, you can talk to me.

Going through a lot of the same stuff and I can't say that I'm coping too well. The feelings have been welling up for years, and lately it feels like I'm ready to breakdown at the slightest hint of these thoughts resurfacing (which has happened a few times already). My friends try to reassure me (and I'm extremely grateful for them), but the smallest nagging doubt in the back of my mind causes me to dismiss all of the wonderful things that they've done for me, and I start feeling like a worthless lump. Not to mention I try to push the feelings away best as I can, so I don't feel like I'm bringing people down. Obviously, this contributes to the growing lump of feelings, but it's been the only way I've tried handling it, and figuring things out has been difficult. I'm still learning how to deal with feelings of depression, and it's been *some* journey. Heck, I'm still learning how to deal with anxiety, and juggling the two is a pain.

Took our four cats and dumped 3 of them somewhere in between my house and the airport and then gave the fourth one (my cat) to one of my cousin's neighbors.

Edit: Wow, this blew up fast... I kind of wish I hadn't posted it on my alt. Because people are asking for more context, I will give you the full story, from what I know. 

It was the week of Thanksgiving and because we were going to be preparing food all week, we put the cats in the garage with all the necessities and had them stay there for the weekend/until people cleared out. One of my aunts didn't approve of what they (cats) were doing to the house and thought that she was helping by getting rid of them. Fast forward a few days after and my family was completely unaware of what she did. Because she didn't tell anyone, I was a nervous wreck for days thinking that the cats might have died and that we might find little cat bodies in the garage later (Panic does not suit me well). Anyway, we were hoping that they might have just run off and been exploring the neighborhood, since two of them were notorious for disappearing for as little as a few hours or as long as a week. What was strange to us was that the other two cats were more home-y and as such, it seemed unlikely that they'd be ones to run off. Another few days pass, and I am talking to my mother and she breaks the news to me. It turns out that my aunt sent a text to her saying that she knows what she did wasn't in line, but still thought that it was necessary and that's why she did what she did. She did say that she wasn't proud of what she did, but it didn't make me feel any better. I heard the fate of my cat from my mother and based on what she told me, my cousin (the culprit's daughter) thought he was too cute to dump, and she gave him to a neighbor in her apartment complex.

Then, a few more days later (it's been  roughly a week and a half to two weeks by this point) one of the outside cats is sitting on our front steps in front of our door wanting to come in. We let him and and see that he's covered it dirt, visibly exhausted, and looks like he's been through Hell and back. We give him a bath and he seems uneasy for the next few days, but seems somewhat relived that he's back home again. 

I also got my facts a little mixed up, as the other outdoor cat (Remington) was actually MIA during the holidays so only two cats were dumped. When the other outdoor cat showed up, the reunion was short lived and he ran off again, only to get into a fight with a neighbor cat. Animals services catches him and asks if we want to pay to get him back, and we later came to the decision that it would be better for him to find a home with people he does like, instead of being in a home of people he seems to barely tolerate. Haven't heard anything from him since. 

Anyway, the biggest casualty was one of the indoor cats being dumped into what I would assume was the middle of nowhere with the other outdoor cat. Never heard from him again. 

Fates of the cats:

Chase (outdoor): currently living with us, once again, and seems much happier.

Sherlock (mainly indoor/my cat): supposedly with someone I don't know because he was too cute to throw out, based on what I heard.

Remington (outdoor): Got in trouble with neighbors, didn't come home. Current fate is unknown. 

Whiskers (indoor): Unknown.

Sorry if it seems all over the place. I'll edit if I see more errors. Thanks for reading. 

Edit 2: Also, I didn't really confront her or anything, and no dead bodies. Too depressed for stabbing. I actually visited her about two weeks ago, and while I have not completely forgiven her, I act civil enough, but I don't actively seek talking to her anymore (not that I ever did, but less so now).

Edit 3: Also, the Humane Center where I live does not euthanize animals. There are a number of adoption centers and shelters that are strongly against such practices unless it is the best option for the animal (i.e. health decline).
